signals.title: NOK/NZD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Energy Shock
signals.text: NOK leads G10 performance at +1.681% across 2 pairs, while NZD lags at −0.862% across 4 pairs, establishing a 2.543% spread that triggers the critical bilateral theme threshold. The divergence is reinforced by Strait of Hormuz naval mine detonations and tanker disruptions sending WTI to $104.1/bbl, providing terms-of-trade support to the petro-currency while weighing on cyclical commodity importers. The ESI spread corroborates the divergence, with NOK printing +14.9 against NZD's −17.1. Relative monetary policy provides nominal backing via Norges Bank at 4.50% against RBNZ at 2.75%, delivering a +175bp rate advantage to NOK. Trade bias: Bullish NOK/NZD; energy terms-of-trade divergence and +175bp policy advantage support continued upside. Catalyst: New Zealand Employment Change at 21:45 UTC. Risk: Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes reopen without incident, unwinding the crude risk premium.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.52, holding below its SMA20 of 157.90 and above its SMA50 of 157.41 within an established broader downtrend structure. While Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% maintains a +275bp carry buffer, the options market exhibits intense downside protection demand with 25d risk reversals printing at −2.24 (Saxo, 1M tenor, indicative mid). This sharp put skew conflicts directly with CFTC spec positioning, where JPY net shorts stand at −19,224 contracts (pctl 94, z +1.57), signaling that institutional options desks are heavily hedging against a sharp downside move. VRP sits at +1.9% with IV at 7.4% against HV30 at 5.5%, demonstrating that forward-looking event risk remains priced at a premium. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; severe options downside skew indicates asymmetric unwind risk against crowded carry positioning. Catalyst: US ISM Manufacturing PMI at 15:00 UTC. Risk: Spot clears and closes above the SMA200 at 158.53, invalidating the technical ceiling.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short + Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1166, remaining structurally heavy below its SMA20 (1.1201), SMA50 (1.1392), and SMA200 (1.1563) in a confirmed downtrend. CFTC speculative accounts hold an extreme net short position of −99,557 contracts (pctl 2, z −1.78) following a WoW reduction of −5,419 contracts. Concurrently, retail positioning on Retail sentiment data is 86% long, creating an institutional-versus-retail divergence at an extreme decile. The underlying rate architecture sustains fundamental downward pressure via Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65%, providing a +135bp carry advantage to the dollar, alongside an OIS SOFR-€STR spread of +150bp. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; persistent +135bp carry deficit and retail crowding favor downside continuation toward lower bounds. Catalyst: Germany Retail Sales at 07:00 UTC. Risk: A daily close above the SMA20 at 1.1201 triggers short-covering among extended institutional positions.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Technical Resistance at Moving Average Cluster
signals.text: AUD/USD prints at 0.7026, holding above its SMA20 at 0.6996 but encountering tight overhead resistance against the SMA200 at 0.7060 and SMA50 at 0.7069. Intraday price action reflects a counter-trend attempt inside a broader macro downtrend, with the steep 200-day average leaning against upward momentum. CFTC positioning shows speculative leveraged funds net long +43,927 contracts (pctl 50, z +0.27), indicating balanced institutional exposure following a WoW reduction of −3,679 contracts. The pair retains carry backing with RBA at 4.60% vs Fed 4.00% delivering a 60bp cash rate premium and an AONIA-SOFR OIS differential of 66bp favoring the Aussie. Trade bias: Range-bound AUD/USD; 60bp carry advantage is capped by the 0.7060/0.7069 moving average barrier. Catalyst: RBA Interest Rate Decision at 04:30 UTC. Risk: A clean break above 0.7069 confirms trend reversal and forces momentum chasing toward 0.7150.
